defects.evidence: foundry_prepare.version_one_jobs: `if campaign: job.pop('allowed_tools', None)` / `return projected`; prepare uses `jobs=version_one_jobs(jobs, args.campaign)` then only `plan.update(..., jobs=jobs)` inside the campaign branch; test_campaign_preparation_strips_then_restores_only_v3_tool_policy asserts campaign=False equality with original jobs including any allowed_tools.
defects.reason: Non-campaign preparation only strips allowed_tools when campaign is truthy; version_one_jobs(jobs, False) returns jobs unchanged, so input jobs that already contain allowed_tools can pass validate_plan and be emitted on the v2 path even though docs claim refuse-at-prepare and runtime worker_allowed_tools then Refuses—v2 compatibility is fail-closed late, not preparation-clean.

defects.evidence: `def collect_filing(..., allowed_tools=TOOL_NAMES)` plus `disallowed = sorted(set(call_names) - set(allowed_tools))`; only the shown foundry_client call site passes `allowed_tools=allowed_tools`; job['allowed_tools'] is not read inside collect_filing.
defects.reason: collect_filing defaults allowed_tools=TOOL_NAMES, so any missed or future caller silently qualifies the full foundry surface and never raises the new CompletedFailure allowlist path—policy enforcement is caller-optional rather than packet-derived.

defects.evidence: devin_tools builds `allow: [f'mcp__foundry__{n}' for n in allowed_tools]` and prompt `'Your exact allowed foundry tools are: ' + ','.join(allowed_tools)`; serve_connection uses `definitions(broker.allowed_tools)`; new tests cover definitions(broker.allowed_tools), broker.call denial, collect_filing CompletedFailure, and worker_allowed_tools, but not prompt text, config.json allow list, or tools/list over serve_connection.
defects.reason: Obligation checklist items for prompt/config alignment and tools/list filtering are implemented but not directly tested; coverage stops at Broker.call denial, definitions() unit filter, and collect_filing CompletedFailure—insufficient evidence that provider_config allow, prompt enumeration, and serve_connection tools/list stay coupled to the same allowlist.

defects.evidence: TOOL-PIPELINE.md: “required `allowed_tools` list”; validate_allowed_tools allows empty list; test_v3_requires_machine_enforced_job_tool_policy does `tool_free['jobs'][0]['allowed_tools'] = []; validate(tool_free)`; worker_allowed_tools empty → `()`.
defects.reason: Docs say a v3 job uses the required allowed_tools list as an explicit subset, while validation and tests accept allowed_tools=[] as a successful native v3 job—easy to misread as “non-empty required.”

defects.evidence: Broker.call writes request with `number: self.count` then `if name not in self.allowed_tools: result = {'ok': False, 'error': 'tool not permitted for this job'}` else sets `self.uncertain = True`; test_job_tool_allowlist_filters_discovery_and_receipts_denial expects two receipts and `assertFalse(broker.uncertain)` after denial.
defects.reason: Disallowed broker calls still allocate request numbers/receipts before denial and do not set uncertain; correct for CompletedFailure qualification, but max_calls/receipt budget can be exhausted by denied probes without an explicit test or doc note.

required_checks: Against candidate_base 7d1cb22403d4a63e28b7628701eef889e2beefcf: confirm pre-diff job key checks, Broker.call uncertain/receipt ordering, and all collect_filing call sites so the TOOL_NAMES default cannot bypass policy.

Refuse or strip allowed_tools during non-campaign/v2 prepare before validate_plan emits a plan; add a regression test that input jobs with allowed_tools without --campaign do not produce a durable v2 plan.
Add tests that restricted allowed_tools appear identically in prompt.md, config.json permissions.allow, MCP tools/list via serve_connection, and Broker denial receipts.
Re-run the claimed Windows full construction suite, Ruff, and git diff --check on the exact committed tree; do not treat observed_checks as verified.
Confirm no other packet consumers require an exact key set that would break on additive plan_version.

Live/provider probes remain out of scope until unit/ruff/plan/tool-policy gates pass; any Devin probe must still demand SWE-2 Max identity, foundry-only calls, broker correspondence, normal exit, and quiescent cleanup before wave scale.
reservations: Embedded diff, proposal_sha256, and observed_checks are untrusted; this review did not read the reference tree, run tests, or execute code.

Foreign/native tools, model drift, broker/export divergence, and cleanup uncertainty remain correctly Refused only insofar as the surrounding pre-diff collect_filing gates are unchanged—those bodies are not fully present in the proposal hunks.
CLI permissions.allow is still presentation-layer; OS containment and receipt qualification remain the real evidence boundary, as the doc addendum states.
Empty allowlist jobs can validate and launch with zero MCP tools; that is fail-closed for tool use but may still produce message-only completions—product intent not proven from the packet alone.
No scientific execution, auth/config/autonomy change, publication, merge, or integration authorization is implied by this review.
strengths: v3 campaign validation requires exact job key set including allowed_tools and runs validate_allowed_tools, blocking brief-only or omitted tool policy at plan validate time.
write_file is coupled to develop + non-empty allowed_paths, and writable jobs must include write_file—machine policy, not prose.
worker_allowed_tools preserves full TOOL_NAMES for non-v3 and Refuses allowed_tools on non-v3 packets; packet_for adds plan_version so v3 policy is selectable without relying on job shape alone.

Broker filters tools/list via definitions(allowed_tools), denies disallowed calls with a durable receipt, and skips setting uncertain on denial so cleanup/provenance gates are not spuriously poisoned.

collect_filing keeps Refused for uncertain broker, non-zero/unclean transport, model drift, non-foundry tools, and export↔receipt divergence; only after those gates does matched allowlist violation become CompletedFailure—matches the obligation packet.
Projection strips allowed_tools for the shared v1 contract path (foundry validate projection and prepare version_one_jobs when campaign) then restores original jobs for native v3.
review.summary: The diff correctly layers v3 per-job allowlists (exact job keys, tools/list filter, broker denial without uncertain, provider allow/prompt alignment) and preserves Refused for native/drift/divergence/cleanup while mapping matched disallowed foundry calls to CompletedFailure only after normal-completion gates; it is not yet lead-ready because non-campaign prepare may still carry allowed_tools into v2-shaped plans, collect_filing defaults to the full TOOL_NAMES surface, and prompt/config/MCP list alignment lack direct tests—base 7d1cb224 and observed Windows gates were not independently verified.
